name: Abū Tammām Ḥabīb ibn Aws al-Ṭāʾī
summary: Poet of Syrian origin who began as a water-carrier in the mosque of Fusṭāṭ, learned among the men of letters, and compiled the anthology al-Ḥamāsa, read and commented on by the grammarians.
bio: Ibn al-Anbārī tells that Abū Tammām, of Syrian origin, carried water in the congregational mosque in Egypt as a youth, sat with the men of letters and learned from them, and worked at poetry until he mastered it.
He praised the caliph al-Muʿtaṣim and his generals and died in 231/846 (some say 232). His anthology of old poetry, al-Ḥamāsa, became a school text, commented on by al-Marzūqī and al-Tibrīzī.

sources.title: Ibn al-Anbārī, Nuzhat al-alibbāʾ fī ṭabaqāt al-udabāʾ (Cairo 1294/1877), pp. 213–216
